FINISH STORY #403: one coverage gap that points at the #394 merge. Branch story-403-process-tree, already checked out in this worktree (HEAD edf539c7, rebased onto main e12f24f1 by rebase-and-finish-story-403-a-ti-68e13bf2, which ruled clean). Keep everything that round did.

The controller's exact-coverage gate is short by one line and one branch: crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine.rs:571 and BRDA 569,0,1, in Engine::drive. That is the arm where lawful_end_under_contention returns Ok(None), which it does only after land_held_outcome (engine.rs, around lines 667-669) lands a HELD outcome: a terminal event whose append the lock outlasted, held by append_raw under #394.

On main (e12f24f1) the arm is covered, by #394's a_terminal_event_the_lock_outlasts_lands_its_real_outcome_in_the_lawful_end (engine/contention_tests.rs). On this branch that test still PASSES, but the arm is not reached. So the terminal event now lands by another route, most likely because the rebase's merge of #394's Settled::outcome with #403's report.refused/settled_outcome changed where, or whether, append_raw holds the terminal event.

Do exactly this:
1. Establish the cause. Instrument locally (not committed) or read the paths. Say in notes which route the test's terminal event takes on this branch, and which on main (git show e12f24f1:crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine.rs).
2. If the merge lost #394's hold-and-land-in-the-lawful-end behaviour, restore it, so a terminal event the lock outlasts is held by append_raw and landed by the lawful end. That behaviour was ruled by the operator on 2026-09-28 (the bounded settlement, decision 0029's proposed addendum). #403's received/refused/cleanup fields must still be carried on that path.
3. Make the test bind the path, not just the end state. Assert that the outcome was landed by the lawful end, for example by asserting what only that route produces (the event order, the cause, or a held-outcome marker), so the test fails if the terminal event lands by another route. Add a compiling removal control: make land_held_outcome's caller skip it, and see the test fail.
4. Check with `cargo +$(cat rust-nightly-version.txt) llvm-cov -p brokkr-runtime --lib --branch --lcov -- contention` (the pinned nightly), and quote engine.rs's DA:571 and BRDA:569 lines in notes.

Gates, all clean, from the worktree root: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test -p brokkr-protocol -p brokkr-runtime; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib --test suppressions --test hands; typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files and clones; git diff --check origin/main..HEAD. Tests need GIT_CONFIG_COUNT and GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0 unset if they touch git. Keep each function's CC within the complexity ratchet. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh. Run everything in the foreground, and never end your turn with a background job or a scheduled wake-up pending.

Commit: one commit, signed off (git commit -s), message "<area>: <what changed> (#403)", ending with "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>". Never push. Every claim in your notes points to a command you ran and what it printed.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read. The ruled #403 residuals are not findings.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

result.notes: CAUSE (step 1). The merge lost nothing. The engine's hold-and-land path is byte-identical to main: I extracted drive+lawful_end_under_contention+land_held_outcome (main e12f24f1 lines 505-661 vs HEAD 558-714) and append_raw (main 826-870 vs HEAD 879-923) and `diff` printed DRIVE_LAWFUL_IDENTICAL and APPEND_RAW_IDENTICAL. The route is decided by timing. The old test released the peer's lock 4.5 patiences (900 ms) after the driver's `exited` signal. The terminal event is held only if its 3 patiences (600 ms) run out first, so the engine must reach the terminal append within 300 ms of the driver's exit. On main nothing slow sits in that window, and in main's code the test takes the held route. On this branch #403's protocol::process::tree::end (new file, absent at e12f24f1: `git show e12f24f1:.../tree.rs` -> 'exists on disk, but not in e12f24f1') sits in that window: a process-table read, the group kill and the reap, under attempts.rs's process-global registry lock, which the 100 ms TRACK thread also takes. Instrumented (eprintln, not committed): on an idle host the branch still takes the held route: `exited` at .242983753, EffectSucceeded append starts at .285563498 (~43 ms later), three tries, `append_raw end EffectSucceeded +602.86ms ok=false`, `lawful_end held=true`, lands on its 2nd try. The pinned-nightly gate command covered the arm here both serially (DA:571,1; BRDA:569,0,1,1) and in parallel (same). So the controller's gap did not reproduce idle. I reproduced it by slowing tree::end by 350 ms (temporary sleep, reverted): the OLD test still PASSED ('1 passed') but engine.rs showed DA:571,0 and BRDA:569,0,1,- (the terminal event landed by its own patiences, no hold). I infer, and did not observe, that the controller's loaded full run pushed the terminal append past the 300 ms margin the same way. STEP 2: no production behaviour to restore; append_raw still holds and the lawful end still lands, and #403's refused/cleanup fields ride on the report before the terminal payload is built, which is unchanged. STEP 3: drive() is now `self.drive_racing(|_| {})`. The new private drive_racing takes a `before_lawful_end: impl FnMut(&EngineError)` closure that sees each error a turn ends on before the lawful end is tried. This is the house's *_racing closure-seam form (operator_command_racing/conclude_racing), not a trait (ruling 2). The test now takes the lock before the seat's result (slot filled before `locked` is signalled) and drops it only in that closure, so the success can land by no route but the lawful end. It asserts `lawful_ends == [true]` (met exactly once, on StoreError::Contended{operation:"append"}) plus the existing event order [Requested, Started, Succeeded], no 'journal contention', AwaitingOperator. Patience is 50 ms; no clock decides the route. REMOVAL CONTROL: adding `&& effect_id.is_empty()` to land_held_outcome's caller filter (engine.rs lawful end) made a_terminal_event_the_lock_outlasts_lands_its_real_outcome_in_the_lawful_end FAIL: 'left: [EffectRequested, EffectStarted, EffectIndeterminate] right: [EffectRequested, EffectStarted, EffectSucceeded]'. Restored, passes. With the 350 ms tree::end slowdown the NEW test still reached the arm (DA:584,1; BRDA:582,0,1,1). STEP 4: `cargo +nightly-2026-09-05 llvm-cov -p brokkr-runtime --lib --branch --lcov -- contention` (24 passed). The old DA:571/BRDA:569 lines moved by 13 into drive_racing; engine.rs record: DA:582,4 DA:583,1 DA:584,1; BRDA:582,0,0,1 and BRDA:582,0,1,1 (the old 571/569). GATES: cargo fmt --check FMT_OK; clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings finished clean; cargo test -p brokkr-protocol -p brokkr-runtime: zero result lines with failures (runtime lib 517 passed, protocol lib 500 passed/1 ignored); cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib --test suppressions --test hands: 494/10/6 passed (1 ignored); typos --hidden TYPOS_OK; quality/ratchet.sh files 'file size holds'; clones 'duplication holds'; git diff --check origin/main..HEAD DIFF_CHECK_OK; bundles/self compiled. Committed 0c9df16f, signed off, not pushed. scripts/coverage-exact.sh was not run, as instructed: the controller's exact-coverage verdict is pending. Sandbox note: `unset GIT_CONFIG_*` needed approval and was not run; the tests passed as run. FOLLOW-UP (not fixed): the old test's clock-based shape may exist in other end-to-end contention tests (a_lock_that_outlasts_both_windows..., a_finished_seats_terminal_event_waits_out...), which also depend on tree::end's duration.

The route is decided by timing: process.rs finish() calls tree::end (process.rs:312) before AttemptReport is returned and the terminal append runs, so #403's process-table read/group kill/reap sits between the driver's exit and the terminal append. result.notes:
Review chief, panel result 'clean' (correctness clean, adversarial clean). Neither member's notes addressed the gate or argued for a result; both reported evidence, and I re-verified the load-bearing claims myself before ruling. Floor: clean; my own read finds nothing above info.
